title: Former JROTC teacher at TC Roberson pleads guilty to indecent liberties charge - NewsBreak
text:
By Kara Fohner ,
1 days ago This article has been updated to correct a reporting error.
ASHEVILLE - A former Asheville-area teacher was sentenced to probation on a charge of indecent liberties with a child.
Michael Roy McCrea, 62, of Fletcher, was arrested Nov. 18, 2024, and accused of behaving inappropriately with a student who was under the age of 16.
The warrant listed the date of offense as Nov. 8. McCrea was a JROTC instructor at TC Roberson High School in South Asheville and the victim was a student at the school when the offense happened, the warrant states.
McCrea was a retired Master Sgt. who served in the U.S. Air Force for 21 years, according to previous Citizen Times reporting. He began working as a Junior ROTC instructor at TC Roberson in October 2018, according to Ken Ulmer, a spokesperson for Buncombe County Schools. McCrea served in the U.S. Air Force for 21 years, according to his LinkedIn profile.
McCrea taught at the school until Nov. 13, 2024, when the Sheriff's Office began its investigation after a notification from school administrators, according to both the Sheriff's Office and the school district. He was arrested five days later, but he posted a $15,000 secured bond the same day and was released from the Buncombe County Detention Facility.
McCrea pleaded guilty March 23 to a single felony charge of indecent liberties with a child, according to court records. His 16–29-month prison sentence was suspended, and he was placed on two years of supervised probation. Superior Court Judge Louis Trosch Jr also ordered that McCrea register as a sex offender and have no contact with the victim in the case.
McCrea declined to comment. His lawyer, Doug Edwards, issued a statement, saying, "Mr. McCrea has accepted responsibility for having inappropriate conversations with a student via messaging applications. While that conduct breaches the law and was taken seriously, at no point was he accused of committing any physical or contact offense against a student."
Kara Fohner is the Public Safety Reporter for the Asheville Citizen Times. Email her at kfohner@usatodayco.com or follow her on X at @karafohner.
